## Arithmetic sequences and their graphs {#ss3-graph .ap-lesson .ap-graph-slide}

What changes when we change the first term or the common difference?

<div data-module="arithmetic-graph" class="arithmetic-graph" aria-label="Explore an arithmetic sequence and its generating line"></div>

::: notes

Default a=2,d=5, matching Example 3.4(a). The first eight terms appear as separate points. The blue point is the first term at n=1. Change a while holding d fixed, then change d while holding a fixed. Keep the vertical scale fixed so changes in gradient are comparable.
Show generating line reveals the orange continuous line, its equation, gradient and an open marker at the y-intercept (0,a−d). The intercept marker is not a sequence term. The view shows a segment of the generating line, which continues beyond the window. Presets: Increasing (2,5), Decreasing (20,−3), Constant (7,0). Presets and sliders preserve line visibility; Reset returns to (2,5) and hides the line. Values range a=−10…30,d=−6…6, with eight displayed positive integer inputs.
Use the decreasing and constant presets as previews, then let students complete the following booklet subparts. Students can revisit this slide with Previous or the slide map; activity state is preserved.

:::
